GitHub documentation evidence, retrieved 2026-11-21.
REST API version shown in the published examples: 2026-03-10.
Quoted fragments are in quotation marks; other text summarizes their context.

Add parameters and ownership
https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/sub-issues#add-sub-issue
The request example uses POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/sub_issues.
The body parameter table requires the integer "sub_issue_id", identifying the
child issue by its global id. It also offers the optional boolean "replace_parent"
to move an existing relationship. The ownership requirement is explicit:
"The sub-issue must belong to the same repository owner as the parent issue".
The published issue example has id 1 and number 1347, illustrating the distinction.

Hierarchy limits
https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/adding-sub-issues
"You can add up to 100 sub-issues per parent issue and create up to eight levels of nested sub-issues."

Fine-grained token permissions
https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/sub-issues#fine-grained-access-tokens-for-get-parent-issue
https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/sub-issues#fine-grained-access-tokens-for-list-sub-issues
Both read endpoints list: '"Issues" repository permissions (read)'.
https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/sub-issues#fine-grained-access-tokens-for-add-sub-issue
The add endpoint lists: '"Issues" repository permissions (write)'.
These sections cover fine-grained personal tokens and GitHub App user and
installation tokens; public relationship reads can be unauthenticated.
https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/issues#fine-grained-access-tokens-for-update-an-issue
The update endpoint includes '"Issues" repository permissions (write)' among
its accepted permission sets. This supplies permission to update issue bodies.
